newsitem.title: USA: U.S. rig count down 3 to 815 in latest week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. rig count down 3 to 815 in latest week.

text.p: The number of rigs exploring for oil and natural gas in the United States stood at 815 as of Jan. 24, down three from the prior week and 112 above the year-ago total of 703, Baker Hughes Inc. reported Friday.
The number of rigs drilling on land remained at 685, while rigs working offshore fell three to 107. The number of rigs active in inland waters remained 23.
Among the individual states, the biggest changes occurred in Texas, which was up 11, Ohio, which was down seven and Louisiana, which was down five.
A total of 333 rigs were exploring for crude oil, down two from last week. The number of rigs searching for gas was down one at 481, while the number of miscellaneous drilling projects remained one.
In Canada, the number of working rigs was up five at 415 vs. 355 a year ago.
The weekly rig count reflects the number of rigs exploring for oil and gas, not those producing oil and gas.

Separately, Offshore Data Services said there were 162 rigs under contract in the U.S. Gulf as of Jan. 24, stable from a week ago. The utilization rate for rigs working in the Gulf, based on a total fleet of 183, was 88.5 percent.
The number of working rigs in the European/Mediterranean area also remained at 105 rigs under contract out of a total fleet of 106, a utilization rate of 99.1 pct.
The worldwide rig count remained the same at 557 out of a total fleet of 606, making the utilization rate 91.9 percent.
